outcome.technical: _locks.py: _is_zombie(pid) now returns (True|False|None, reason). None means the state could not be read: ps would not start (the OSError is named with its errno, e.g. PermissionError (EPERM)), exited non-zero ('ps exited 71'), timed out, or printed nothing. HEAD ignored ps's exit code and returned False on OSError. New public liveness(pid) returns {alive, state, basis}, where state is running|gone|zombie|unverified|unknown. A present pid whose state is unreadable is state 'unverified', alive True, and its basis names the refusal. pid_alive(pid) is liveness(pid)['alive'], so its values are unchanged from HEAD in every case (unverified stays True and is never None), and the age fallback is never reached on a refusal. judge() reads liveness(); on 'unverified' it returns (True, '<basis> on this host (<host>)') before age is asked, so acquire's E_LIVE 'basis:' line names the refusal. errno import added. _parent_of is not changed: on a refusal it still returns None, which ends the ancestry walk; that walk only adds a sentence to a refusal and never decides one. tests/_harness.py: added ps_refusal() (an independent ps probe of this process, returning the refusal worded or None), state_refusal() (None where /proc/<pid>/stat exists, else ps_refusal()), with_stub_ps(fn, script) (puts a stub ps first on PATH, or with script=None makes it the only, unexecutable ps; PATH restored in finally), and recorded(fn) (runs a block against a capturing check). test__locks.py: the zombie block is now _zombie_cases(). pz0 and pz0b (the formerly unlabelled pid_alive case) skip through _harness.skip with state_refusal()'s text as evidence, and only when that independent probe reports a refusal. ap3 skips the same way. New zr-block zr1-zr6. test_run_test_gate.py: lv0 is split into lv1 (a single pid; skips on state_refusal), lv2 (the group; skips on ps_refusal), lv3 (the static single-look scan, always runs) and lv4 (the lv1/lv2 waits run under a stub ps that exits 71: both skip naming 'exited 71', or lv2 alone where /proc answers, and none fail). test__affected_tests.py: the unguarded ps readers are gone. af38 and af43 now judge their grandchildren with _harness.gone_within, the product's rule through the deadline helper, and the test-local _pid_alive is deleted. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the _locks.py section names liveness and the unverified reading. Runs: test__locks 154/154 plain (exit 0). Under sandbox-exec with '(version 1)(allow default)': 154/154 (exit 0) with pz0, pz0b and ap3 SKIPPED naming 'starting ps raised PermissionError (EPERM: Operation not permitted)'; HEAD's run there had 3 FAILs (pz0, the pid_alive case, ap3). test_run_test_gate --stage lv0: 600/600 plain and sandboxed, with lv1 and lv2 SKIPPED naming EPERM under the sandbox. test__affected_tests: 51/51 plain and sandboxed; HEAD's copy under the sandbox raised PermissionError on 'ps' (45/46). The gate command exited 0: '5/5 files ok, 1124 cases'. First red, before the fix: test__locks at 148/151; zr1 and zr2 failed their assertions (HEAD answered False); zr-block raised AttributeError on liveness, which this task adds. Mutation probes, run in a scratch git-archive export (never the shared tree), each restored and checked with cmp: unverified->None turned zr3 red (153/154); every ps answer None turned pz0b and zr4 red (152/154); judge's unverified branch removed turned zr5 red; refusal->False (HEAD's shape) turned zr1, zr3 and zr5 red (151/154); unverified->gone turned zr3 and zr5 red; judge falling back to age on unverified turned zr5 red (False, 'last touched 125 min old', code 4); _harness.ps_refusal never reporting a refusal turned zr6 red (153/154) and lv4 red (599/600). Dependants: holder_gone reads pid_alive(...) is False, and unverified is True, so a present holder is not gone (unchanged). judge reads liveness() and names the refusal. panel-server._pid_alive (pid_alive is True), _proc_group._gone (poll() first, then pid_alive is False), stamp-verification.py:3230 (True->running), audit-lock.py:146 (an alias of the same object, pinned by b1), tools/_suite.py pid_alive (is True) and tools/prove-gates.py _pid_state (three-valued): all still correct, because pid_alive returns exactly what HEAD returned in every reading. Under a refusal each now still reads the holder as live, which is the conservative direction. tests/_harness._pid_present is unchanged (pid_alive is not False). _group_present still returns True when it cannot enumerate, which is correct (not confirmed gone); lv2 now skips where ps is refused. Other dependants: _evidence_io, _invariants, _proposals, audit-task and merge-manifest import _locks for locks and use none of the changed signatures; the only callers of _is_zombie are _locks.liveness and test__locks (grep). test__affected_tests' names used elsewhere (_suites, _tool_module, _cases, _selftest) are untouched, and the deleted _pid_alive had no outside reader. test_run_test_gate's _group_present and _pid_present readers are unchanged. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE: only the _locks.py section text changed.
outcome.descriptive: When ps is refused (a macOS sandbox), liveness now says 'present, unverified' with the refusal as its basis, a lock holder is not taken over on it, and the zombie/liveness suites skip naming the refusal instead of going red.

tasks.title: The drive dispatches the task gate as a background step and decides from the recorded row, so the CLI's background-command limit cannot kill it into a second measurement
tasks.description: Fixes F838. In stage 2 k02 and k03r the orchestrator's `drive-phase.py next ... --task --signal` call carried no timeout and no run_in_background; the CLI moved it to the background after 120 s and killed it at about 708-720 s (durationMs 708384/708206), and the drive measured the whole gate again. At a27f8a56 the drive runs the task gate inline in gate_step 4573-4594 (task_gate 3311-3322, record_gate 3298-3308). Only the writer's run: line carries a background rule (WRITER_RULE drive-phase.py:475-476, held by sn4d ~10082). Mechanism: a dispatch step for the gate with a WRITER_RULE-shaped rule (every command already routes dispatch to background Bash; commands/phase.md has 2 B left under measure-context, so no command-doc bytes), the next call reuses the recorded verdict (reused_result ~2979, GATE VERDICT REUSED) - verify reuse holds on an identical tree digest - and a wait step for a launched gate with no row yet (like wait-writer 493-497). The CLI's 600 s cap is recorded at audit-task.py:5902 (_BASH_CALL_CAP_SECONDS).

tasks.title: A task's dependants include the documents that name what its files define: prose naming a decision, step or config key a declared file defines is listed, and the three stale passages found in this phase are corrected
tasks.description: Fixes F839, F840, F841 and their class. Three times in P157 a task's change left prose outside its declared files describing the old behaviour: tests/test__doctor_policy.py ~454 says the runner loads skills (P157.3 made it disclose them), plugins/audit/README.md's executor.phaseGateOnly default says every gate command is listed (P157.4 leaves a slow step to the drive), plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md:265 says a recorded-gate red goes back to the session (P157.5 added gate-red-base; P157.6 made the gate a background dispatch). The brief's Who depends on this (status/_impact.py, rendered by audit-lookup.py) names readers by import, path and basename and names used elsewhere in code; it does not name a document that describes a declared file's behaviour by the names that file defines. Extend it to tracked prose: a decision, step or config key defined in a declared file and named in a tracked .md (or a comment) is a dependant, shown under the existing bound with the name it uses. Choose how a defined name is read (decision/step tables, config keys read) by measuring over this tree, and report how many prose dependants a typical brief gains - a section nobody reads is not a mechanism. Then correct the three passages.

add: tests/test__impact.py: a tracked .md naming in backticks a decision, step or config key a declared file defines is listed under that file's dependants with the name it uses; replayed on the three passages this phase left stale - README's executor.phaseGateOnly row, execute-task.md's gate-red-writer line, test__doctor_policy's skills-loaded comment - each is listed for the file whose change made it stale (red-first: none is listed today)
gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__impact.py tests/test_audit_lookup.py tests/test__doctor_policy.py tests/test__output_lints.py tests/test__deps.py tests/test__refs.py tools/_suite.py
